commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] hoist entire chains of set_encoding ops (#24904)

Capture the entire producer chains of `set_encoding` ops, and hoist them
if there is no unhoistable op in the source backward slice. The metadata
backward slice, i.e. the backward slice from the `encoding_dims` can
always be hoisted.

Fixes #24876.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

commit_message:
[ROCM] Add rocjitsu e2e validation

Add a CPU-hosted ROCm e2e test helper for gfx942, gfx950, gfx1100,
gfx1201, and gfx1250. Configure gfx942 in the initial regular CI build
so its test dependencies are ready before simulator testing. Retarget
iree-test-deps for the remaining architectures, reusing the compiler
and runtime binaries.

Install a pinned TheRock nightly with venv and pip in the regular Linux
x64 clang workflow, then pass the initialized SDK and rocjitsu CLI to
the helper. Run after the CPU tests and always upload per-target logs
and JUnit results. Keep dependency installation out of the test helper.

Run one CTest invocation per architecture with eight parallel tests.
Use in-process simulation so each test has its own simulator instead
of sharing a daemon's workers. Let CTest handle progress, diagnostics,
per-test timeouts, and JUnit output, with a watchdog around each session.
Propagate configure/build failures so stale artifacts cannot produce a
successful run.

Make the default native-test timeout configurable and label tests that
are too expensive to simulate. Keep those tests enabled for hardware
runs. Exclude TopK v2 from ROCm tests because its missing thread
distribution causes overlapping output writes on all five targets.

Use the target's preferred subgroup size when an executable does not
specify one, so gfx1250 defaults to wave32. Add regression coverage for
the default and explicit subgroup sizes.

Assisted-by: codex

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] `vlen` attribute for DataTiledMMAAttr for RISCV + FP16 port (#24858)

For RISC-V, the vector length per SIMD register is not fixed and is configurable. Therefore, the tile shape of an intrinsic and the total SIMD register bit budget is also parameterized by the vector length. In order for all of these vector length configurations to share a single intrinsic and not duplicate it per-configurable-vlen, we add a `vlen` parameter to the `DataTiledMMAAttr`, which in combination with the intrinsic itself gives the exact shape information, as well as the register budget. These are derived from the `+zvl*b` flags.

Furthermore, add materialization for data-tiled f16 matmul encodings to `iree_codegen.inner_tiled` on RISC-V V targets with Zvfh, as the first consumer of the `vlen` attribute parameter. Lowering to LLVM intrinsics
is not included.

Towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24311

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] hoist entire chains of set_encoding ops (#24904)

Capture the entire producer chains of `set_encoding` ops, and hoist them
if there is no unhoistable op in the source backward slice. The metadata
backward slice, i.e. the backward slice from the `encoding_dims` can
always be hoisted.

Fixes #24876.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] `vlen` attribute for DataTiledMMAAttr for RISCV + FP16 port (#24858)

For RISC-V, the vector length per SIMD register is not fixed and is configurable. Therefore, the tile shape of an intrinsic and the total SIMD register bit budget is also parameterized by the vector length. In order for all of these vector length configurations to share a single intrinsic and not duplicate it per-configurable-vlen, we add a `vlen` parameter to the `DataTiledMMAAttr`, which in combination with the intrinsic itself gives the exact shape information, as well as the register budget. These are derived from the `+zvl*b` flags.

Furthermore, add materialization for data-tiled f16 matmul encodings to `iree_codegen.inner_tiled` on RISC-V V targets with Zvfh, as the first consumer of the `vlen` attribute parameter. Lowering to LLVM intrinsics
is not included.

Towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24311

Assisted-by: Claude Code

[LLVMCPU] `vlen` attribute for DataTiledMMAAttr for RISCV + FP16 port (#24858)

For RISC-V, the vector length per SIMD register is not fixed and is configurable. Therefore, the tile shape of an intrinsic and the total SIMD register bit budget is also parameterized by the vector length. In order for all of these vector length configurations to share a single intrinsic and not duplicate it per-configurable-vlen, we add a `vlen` parameter to the `DataTiledMMAAttr`, which in combination with the intrinsic itself gives the exact shape information, as well as the register budget. These are derived from the `+zvl*b` flags.

Furthermore, add materialization for data-tiled f16 matmul encodings to `iree_codegen.inner_tiled` on RISC-V V targets with Zvfh, as the first consumer of the `vlen` attribute parameter. Lowering to LLVM intrinsics
is not included.

Towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24311

Assisted-by: Claude Code

---------

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] hoist entire chains of set_encoding ops (#24904)

Capture the entire producer chains of `set_encoding` ops, and hoist them
if there is no unhoistable op in the source backward slice. The metadata
backward slice, i.e. the backward slice from the `encoding_dims` can
always be hoisted.

Fixes #24876.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@6cce5bca3b90 (#24912)

* Add prop-dict to IREE operations for strict property assembly formats
introduced by llvm/llvm-project#196269 and enabled for Transform by
llvm/llvm-project#217290.
* Preserve StableHLO's bare enum syntax after llvm/llvm-project#220608
changed EnumAttr's default assembly format to angle brackets.
* Replace deprecated setName() calls with setSymbolName() following
llvm/llvm-project#218921.
* Cherry-pick e45b19d32e7c (llvm/llvm-project#222395) to fix the missing
RemarkStreamer Bazel dependency exposed by llvm/llvm-project#222300.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Add an option to block matmul producers from being fused in the same dispatch region (#24899)

When targeting CPU with data tiling and ukernels enabled (`mmt4d`
specifically), some producers materialize on the stack when fused
together with the consuming matmuls, which may lead to stack oveflow.

This PR adds a workaround/flag which would block fusion of such ops.

The flag is on by default, no performance regressions observed.

### Alternatives considered

At the level of dispatch creation it is not possible to precisely
calculate whether the producer would overflow the stack or not since
there is not enough information at that point. It is possible to
implement a crude approximation, but it heavily depends on the exact
tiling and vectorizing details lower on the stack.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Alex Denisov <denisov@roofline.ai>

[DispatchCreation] Add an option to block matmul producers from being fused in the same dispatch region (#24899)

When targeting CPU with data tiling and ukernels enabled (`mmt4d`
specifically), some producers materialize on the stack when fused
together with the consuming matmuls, which may lead to stack oveflow.

This PR adds a workaround/flag which would block fusion of such ops.

The flag is on by default, no performance regressions observed.

### Alternatives considered

At the level of dispatch creation it is not possible to precisely
calculate whether the producer would overflow the stack or not since
there is not enough information at that point. It is possible to
implement a crude approximation, but it heavily depends on the exact
tiling and vectorizing details lower on the stack.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Alex Denisov <denisov@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops

Convert the typed PT2E per-tensor and per-channel quantize and
dequantize operations before Torch-to-Linalg expands them. This keeps
affine parameter maps, ranges, and signedness available to later QDQ
optimizations.

Leave operations with dynamic or incompatible metadata for the
existing torch-mlir lowering.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops

Convert the typed PT2E per-tensor and per-channel quantize and
dequantize operations before Torch-to-Linalg expands them. This keeps
affine parameter maps, ranges, and signedness available to later QDQ
optimizations.

Leave operations with dynamic or incompatible metadata for the
existing torch-mlir lowering.

legality checks.

Move quantize operations toward real-valued producers and dequantize
operations toward contraction consumers before rewriting contractions to
integer math.

Reuse reshape expansion and unit-dimension folding for affine QDQ
operations. Handle transpose and zero-pad consumers using explicit
legality checks.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

dequantize operations before Torch-to-Linalg expands them. This keeps
affine parameter maps, ranges, and signedness available to later QDQ
optimizations.

existing torch-mlir lowering.

[Torch] Preserve PT2E quantization as LinalgExt ops

Convert the typed PT2E per-tensor and per-channel quantize and
dequantize operations before Torch-to-Linalg expands them. This keeps
affine parameter maps, ranges, and signedness available to later QDQ
optimizations.

Leave operations with dynamic or incompatible metadata for the
existing torch-mlir lowering.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:

commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Drop a provably zero zero_point from the quantization ops

A dequantize whose zero point is zero is symmetric, and every consumer
benefits from seeing it that way: the QDQ to integer rewrite skips a
whole correction term, and the decomposition skips a subtraction.

Quantizers spell a symmetric zero point as a splat, as an explicit
tensor of zeros, or, once the model is frozen, as a resource blob whose
bytes live outside the attribute. isKnownZero answers a splat from its
one stored element and everything else from raw bytes: for an integer
tensor, all bytes zero is equivalent to all elements zero whatever the
width and packing, so no element is materialized as an APInt and the
resource case needs no per width decoding. Padding bytes can only make
the answer a conservative false.

The element type is not rechecked. The only caller passes a zero_point
the op verifier has already established to be an integer.

zero_point is the only optional operand, so the ops carry no operand
segment attribute and the drop is an in place mutation: clear the
operand, drop its indexing map, remove zp_unsigned. Everything else the
op carries is preserved by construction rather than by an attribute
copy that would have to be revisited whenever an attribute is added.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] hoist entire chains of set_encoding ops (#24904)

Capture the entire producer chains of `set_encoding` ops, and hoist them
if there is no unhoistable op in the source backward slice. The metadata
backward slice, i.e. the backward slice from the `encoding_dims` can
always be hoisted.

Fixes #24876.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
